title: Malaysia & Singapore, from the Malay and Chinese press

stories.text: Negeri Sembilan ruler Tuanku Muhriz publicly rebuked the state's Menteri Besar, telling him not to see him until he withdraws his remarks: "Go away, don't see me, I don't want to see you."
AMK Negeri Sembilan questioned whether UMNO-BN can keep the state stable after the incident, saying the public deserves an explanation.
Melaka state election: BN state chairman Ab Rauf Yusoh says the coalition's candidate list is complete and ready to be announced at any time.
Melaka state election: Amanah has been allocated 8 of the 28 seats Pakatan Harapan will contest.
PAS's Syahir Sulaiman says the party not yet naming a prime minister candidate does not mean it has no one to put forward.
The government is being urged to disclose the terms of former PM Najib Razak's house arrest; his lawyer Shafee Abdullah said this week Najib has received the conditions.
A 23-year-old Universiti Malaya economics student says she faced cyberbullying and threats after a video of her questioning fundraising for Najib went viral, and that she will not back down.

A businessman and his brother have gone to the High Court to challenge MACC notices ordering them to declare assets, after MACC raided their homes on 30 Sept in a probe linked to the Bank Rakyat foundation he once chaired.
stories.source: Sin Chew Daily 星洲日报

stories.text: The Gua Sakyamuni Buddhist cave monastery called for an investigation after its main entrance was blocked; APMC, a YTL subsidiary, defended blocking it.
Human Resources Minister Ramanan says the RM2,000 monthly minimum wage, starting June 2027, was set after weighing its effect on inflation.
Speaking in Tianjin, Deputy PM Zahid Hamidi proposed setting up a World TVET Council with China as its permanent host.
Government spokesman Fahmi Fadzil says checks found no Malaysian plantation companies involved in the forest burning in Indonesia.
Singapore's NEA has issued notices under the Transboundary Haze Pollution Act to 7 companies operating in Indonesia, ordering them to put out fires on their land.

Minister Grace Fu says Singapore's haze may last several more weeks, improving at the earliest in late October or early November when the monsoon shifts, and the PSI could reach hazardous levels before then.
President Tharman leaves tomorrow for a five-day state visit to Sweden, the first by a Singapore president, marking 60 years of diplomatic ties.
